claims.statement: `pnpm dev` (scripts/dev.mjs) is the one-command local development startup: it creates .env from .env.example if missing, generates BRIJIO_PAIRING_TOKEN and MCP_HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN via crypto.randomBytes(32).base64url, spawns the WebSocket server and MCP HTTP server under tsx watch as child processes, polls both /health endpoints (500ms interval, 15s timeout) before printing a readiness banner, restarts crashed children with 2s backoff up to 5 attempts, and on SIGINT/SIGTERM sends SIGTERM to children (SIGKILL after 5s grace).

The dev orchestrator classifies an existing .env as 'configured' (both tokens real — shows masked config, prompts to regenerate unless --yes/CI=true), 'placeholders' (placeholder token values trigger regeneration), or 'incomplete', merges generated values while preserving unrelated keys and comments via writeEnv, and mirrors renamed BRIJIO_* values into legacy BROWSERBRIDGE_* aliases via withCompatibilityAliases.

The WebSocket relay entrypoint (servers/websocket/src/index.ts) reads WEBSOCKET_HOST (default 0.0.0.0) and WEBSOCKET_PORT (default 8787) from env, and createWebSocketServer requires a pairing token (options.pairingToken or BRIJIO_PAIRING_TOKEN/BRIJIO_TOKEN env) — it throws if none is configured, so a token must always be supplied in every deployment mode.

The MCP HTTP server derives its configuration from env: MCP_HTTP_HOST (default 0.0.0.0), MCP_HTTP_PORT (default 8788), MCP_HTTP_PATH (default /mcp, normalized to start with '/'), MCP_HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN (required — empty/whitespace throws 'MCP_HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN is required for MCP HTTP transport.'), MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (comma-separated list), BRIJIO_MCP_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS (default 60000) applied as server.requestTimeout, and BRIJIO_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_BUFFER_MS (default 5000) subtracted from the HTTP timeout to derive the approval timeout (min 1000ms).

GET /health on the WebSocket relay (port 8787) returns 200 with {status:'ok', version, uptimeSeconds, extensions:{count, browsers:[{browserInstanceId,label}]}} computed from live presence state — only sockets in OPEN state with an authenticated browserInstanceId are counted; the same data is exposed programmatically as server.getStatus(). Any other path on that HTTP server returns 404.

GET /health on the MCP HTTP server (port 8788) is unauthenticated and returns 200 with {status:'ok', version, uptimeSeconds, websocket:{url, status:'unknown'}} — the websocket.url is the configured BRIJIO_WS_URL and the relay status is never actively probed by the health handler. All non-health requests require the Authorization: Bearer <MCP_HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN> header (401 unauthorized on failure), a GET/POST/DELETE method (405 otherwise), a matching MCP_HTTP_PATH (404 otherwise), and, when an Origin header is present, an origin in MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS matched exactly or via a '*.'-prefixed host wildcard (403 forbidden_origin otherwise); requests without an Origin header bypass the origin check.

The brijio binary loads .env files in a fallback chain — BRIJIO_ENV_FILE explicit override, then ./.env in the working directory, then ~/.brijio/.env — and applyBrijioEnv copies loaded values into process.env only for keys that are currently unset or blank, so real environment variables take precedence over file values.

The combined `brijio` entry point (servers/mcp/bin/brijio.mjs, bundled by tsup into dist/bin/brijio.js with the `browserbridge` name kept as a deprecated alias) handles subcommand parsing and exits early for help/--version/install/uninstall/start/stop/restart/status/logs/--print-config/--doctor/demo before server startup, auto-generates an ephemeral pairing token and MCP auth token when unset (mirroring the pairing token into legacy BROWSERBRIDGE_* env vars), forces 127.0.0.1 binding in --dev and demo modes, starts the WebSocket server and MCP HTTP server in one process for run mode, prints a startup banner to stderr (never stdout), handles EADDRINUSE with a friendly diagnostic, and performs graceful shutdown of all servers on SIGINT/SIGTERM.

In demo mode, the binary first probes http://127.0.0.1:<wsPort>/health — if a daemon is already running it starts only the demo static server (bound to 0.0.0.0, default port 8789 or BRIJIO_DEMO_PORT/BROWSERBRIDGE_DEMO_PORT) and the banner omits WS/MCP URLs and tokens since they belong to the existing daemon; otherwise it starts the full WS+MCP+demo stack.

`brijio --doctor` runs four checks — config file accessibility, MCP and WebSocket port availability via a bind probe (EADDRINUSE fails), network path detection (Tailscale CLI, mDNS, localhost), and Node.js version (fails below 18) — and exits 1 if any check fails, 0 otherwise.

`brijio --print-config [agent]` emits a copy-paste MCP client config block for a named agent (aliases like 'claude' resolve to canonical names such as claude-desktop), with the config on stdout and hints on stderr; when the MCP auth token was auto-generated the output marks it ephemeral, and the MCP host is the best detected network path (Tailscale IP > mDNS > 127.0.0.1) unless --dev forces localhost.

Network detection (servers/mcp/src/network.ts) probes Tailscale by execing `tailscale status --json` with a 2s timeout, detects a Tailscale IP by scanning interfaces for 100.64.0.0/10, and resolves <hostname>.local via DNS for mDNS; bestHost priority is Tailscale > mDNS > 127.0.0.1, and this drives which URLs appear in the startup banner and --print-config.

The startup banner goes to stderr so stdout stays pipe-clean; in normal run mode it lists every detected reachable address (Local 127.0.0.1, plus Tailscale and mDNS hosts when found) with WS and MCP URLs, labels tokens as [ephemeral] when they were auto-generated, and warns that ephemeral tokens change on restart; --dev mode prints only the 127.0.0.1 URLs.

`pnpm token` (scripts/brijio-token.mjs) prints a single generated pairing token to stdout for manual .env entry, with usage instructions on stderr; both dev orchestrator and the script share scripts/token-utils.mjs, whose generatePairingToken and generateAuthToken return randomBytes(32) in base64url encoding.

The daemon layer (servers/mcp/src/daemon.ts) implements install/uninstall/start/stop/restart/status/logs as subcommands: start/stop/restart wrap launchctl load/unload on darwin and systemctl --user start/stop/restart brijio.service on linux, logs tails ~/.brijio/brijio.log on darwin vs journalctl --user -u brijio.service on linux (with --live mapping to tail -f / journalctl --follow), and status reports daemon loaded state (launchctl list / systemctl is-active) plus WebSocket and MCP health probe results on 127.0.0.1 using ports read from ~/.brijio/.env.

`brijio install [--ws-port N] [--mcp-port N]` creates ~/.brijio/ (config), writes ~/.brijio/.env with BRIJIO_PAIRING_TOKEN and MCP_HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN (generated via randomBytes(32).base64url and persisted with mode 0600; existing tokens and env keys are preserved for idempotent reinstall, and explicit ports override), writes ~/.brijio/.env.example on first install, writes a wrapper script at ~/.brijio/bin/brijio that execs node with the resolved binary path, writes the platform service definition, and symlinks it into ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.redvex.brijio.plist (darwin) or ~/.config/systemd/user/brijio.service (linux), then loads it (launchctl unload+load on darwin, systemctl --user daemon-reload + enable --now on linux).

The macOS LaunchAgent plist (label com.redvex.brijio) sets ProgramArguments to the wrapper binary, WorkingDirectory to ~/.brijio, RunAtLoad and KeepAlive true (start on login, restart on crash), and directs stdout/stderr to ~/.brijio/brijio.log; the Linux systemd user unit sets WorkingDirectory=%h/.brijio, ExecStart=%h/.brijio/bin/brijio, Restart=on-failure with RestartSec=5, EnvironmentFile=%h/.brijio/.env, and WantedBy=default.target — no tokens appear in the service definitions because the .env file is the single source of truth.

`brijio uninstall` unloads the service (launchctl unload, or systemctl --user disable --now plus daemon-reload, with failures tolerated) and removes the service link, but never deletes ~/.brijio/ — config and logs are preserved, and the printed guidance says full removal requires an explicit rm -rf ~/.brijio.
Daemon installation supports only darwin and linux — normalizePlatform throws 'Brijio daemon install does not support <platform> yet' for any other platform, including Windows.

The root Dockerfile is a multi-stage build: stage 1 (node:22-alpine, corepack/pnpm) installs workspace deps filtered to @brijio/mcp and builds the tsup-bundled dist/; stage 2 installs s6-overlay v3.2.0.2 (noarch plus arch-specific tarballs mapped from TARGETARCH), copies only dist/ and package.json (with workspace:* deps stripped before npm install --omit=dev), copies docker/s6-rc.d service definitions, sets ENV defaults, EXPOSEs 8787 and 8788, and uses ENTRYPOINT /init.

Inside the container, s6-overlay runs one longrun service 'brijio' (added to the user bundle contents.d) whose run script cds to /app and execs `node dist/bin/brijio.js` — a single Node process starting both the WebSocket relay and MCP server, not one s6 service per server; token auto-generation and the banner are handled by the Node entry point.

The Dockerfile documents and sets container env defaults: WEBSOCKET_HOST=0.0.0.0, WEBSOCKET_PORT=8787, MCP_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0, MCP_HTTP_PORT=8788, MCP_HTTP_PATH=/mcp, BRIJIO_WEBSOCKET_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:8787 (loopback because both servers share one container network namespace), BRIJIO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=5000; BRIJIO_PAIRING_TOKEN and MCP_HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN default to empty and are auto-generated at first startup, printed to stdout, and ephemeral unless set explicitly.

docker-compose.yml defines three profiles: `runtime` (service brijio building the root Dockerfile, passing through .env values for tokens and BRIJIO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS and mapping ports 8787/8788), `legacy-runtime` (service browserbridge that extends brijio as a transition alias), and `test` (nginx:1.27-alpine serving clients/test-page read-only on TEST_PAGE_PORT, default 8080) — so plain `docker compose up` is the runtime profile and the test page is a separate opt-in service.

The MCP server resolves the relay URL through a renamed-env chain with warnings: BRIJIO_WS_URL is preferred over BROWSERBRIDGE_WEBSOCKET_URL / BRIJIO_WEBSOCKET_URL / WEBSOCKET_URL (defaulting to ws://127.0.0.1:8787); BRIJIO_PAIRING_TOKEN over BROWSERBRIDGE_PAIRING_TOKEN / BRIJIO_TOKEN; BRIJIO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS over BROWSERBRIDGE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS (timeout default 5000); and BRIJIO_BROWSER_INSTANCE_ID over BROWSERBRIDGE_BROWSER_INSTANCE_ID — setting both new and old names with different values logs a preference warning.

The MCP HTTP server instantiates a fresh BrijioMcpServer and StreamableHTTPServerTransport per request (sessionIdGenerator undefined, JSON response mode), connects and handles the request, and always closes the MCP server in a finally block — the MCP endpoint is stateless across requests.

scripts/dev.mjs exports its env helpers (createEnvFromTemplate, readEnv, writeEnv, isPlaceholderToken, classifyEnv, generateConfig, withCompatibilityAliases, healthCheck, printBanner, parseArgs, promptUser) which are unit-tested in scripts/dev.test.mjs; the daemon command parser, install plan, plist/unit builders, and start/stop/restart wrappers are unit-tested in servers/mcp/src/daemon.test.ts; health endpoint shapes are covered in servers/websocket/src/server.test.ts and MCP auth/origin rejection in servers/mcp/src/index.test.ts.

Repository tooling requires Node.js >= 22.0.0 and pnpm >= 9.0.0 (packageManager pnpm@10.32.1), while the shipped binary's bundled output targets node20 and its doctor check only enforces Node >= 18 at runtime.
